newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi sanctions maintained at regular UN review.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi sanctions maintained at regular UN review.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council, as expected, retained sanctions against Iraq on Tuesday at its regular 60-day review, diplomats said.

The blanket sanctions have been in place since Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990. The oil-for-food deal agreed upon this month that allows Iraq to sell $2 billion over six months is an exception to the sanctions.

A prime condition for an easing of the sanctions is a report to the council by the special commission that Iraq has fulfilled all obligations calling for the scrapping of its nuclear, chemical, biological and ballistic missile potential.

On Monday, the council censured Iraq for refusing to allow more than 100 missile engines to be taken abroad for examination by experts and reminded Baghdad of its obligation to comply with Gulf war disarmament resolutions.
